subject: Observic relay replacement — clarification on data egress paths and evidence
messages:
From: Aisha Malik <aisha@observic.io>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Shaw <ben.shaw@finpay.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Upcoming relay partner change — short notice notification

Hi David,

Quick heads up from Observic: on Nov 20 we plan to temporarily route telemetry for your FinPay integration through a short-lived relay provider (EdgeChain) while we finish a configuration migration in our EU cluster. This is purely for observability telemetry (metrics/traces). No customer payload is stored by EdgeChain beyond 72 hours; we use TLS in transit and AES-256 at rest for any queued buffers.

Attached is a short notice and the immediate subprocessor snapshot. We wanted to surface this early to give you time to ask for evidence or block if necessary. Key points:
- Scope: metrics + traces only (no PII, no request/response bodies)
- Jurisdiction: relay endpoint will be in Ireland for the period Nov 20–Nov 27
- Retention: ephemeral buffers up to 72 hours, then auto-delete

If you need SOC2 evidence, encryption attestations, or a dataflow diagram, we can pull the evidence bundle by EOD Nov 18.

Thanks —
Aisha
Aisha Malik
Head of Integrations, Observic
[attachment: observic_temp_relay_changes.pdf]
[attachment: subprocessor_inventory_snapshot_20261115.csv]

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Malik <aisha@observic.io>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Upcoming relay partner change — short notice notification

Thanks for the notice, Aisha — appreciate the advance heads up. A couple of clarifying asks for our security and the FinPay legal team: 

1) Can you confirm absolute data types forwarded to EdgeChain? You mention "metrics + traces" — please confirm there is no request/response body, no headers with user identifiers, and no customer IDs in trace attributes.

2) Please provide the shortest possible evidence set before Nov 18:
   - EdgeChain subprocessor contact and SOC2 type II report (or equivalent)
   - TLS cipher suite details and key management statement for queued buffers
   - Dataflow diagram that shows routing from Observic EU collector -> EdgeChain -> Observic EU region store

3) Because FinPay is subject to contractual geo-residency constraints, confirm that there will be no onward transfer outside of Ireland for any FinPay telemetry and that buffers will be auto-deleted. If EdgeChain performs any processing that might change residency (e.g., forwarding to a third-party analytics endpoint), we will need to treat that as a material subprocessor change.

CC'ing Kimberly (Security) and Lauren (Contracts) to validate acceptance criteria. If possible, we'll aim to sign off before Nov 19.

Regards,
David
David Kim
Head of Customer Security Operations
Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-11-15T13:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Upcoming relay partner change — short notice notification

Hi all,

Thanks for the quick reply — answers inline below and attaching the EdgeChain attestation bundle.

1) Data types: Confirmed. Only numeric metrics and trace IDs/timestamps. We do strip application-level IDs from trace attributes for FinPay customers; no request bodies, no user-visible PII, and no persistent customer IDs are sent.

2) Evidence attached: EdgeChain SOC2-II summary (redacted where necessary), edge-relay-kms-statement.pdf, and a concise dataflow PNG. EdgeChain operates under a contractual DPA with Observic and has a data retention policy of maximum 72 hours for queued buffers.

3) Residency: Observic will not initiate any onward transfer outside Ireland for FinPay telemetry during the Nov 20–27 window. If EdgeChain requires forwarding to any other third party, we will pause the change and notify you.

Attachments: edgechain_attestation_bundle.zip, dataflow_obs_edgechain_ireland.png

Let me know if that covers everything — happy to jump on a quick call Nov 16 if you prefer to walk through the docs.

Best,
Aisha

[attachment: edgechain_attestation_bundle.zip]
[attachment: dataflow_obs_edgechain_ireland.png]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-16T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Observic relay replacement — clarification on data egress paths and evidence

David / Lauren — quick internal note after reviewing the bundle Aisha sent: 

Summary of what we need to clear before sign-off to FinPay:
- Confirm EdgeChain SOC2-II covers network segregation and key management controls (we have the summary; need the auditor's report pages 5-7 redacted).
- Confirm the KMS boundary: who holds the encryption keys for the ephemeral buffers? If EdgeChain holds keys, need to see their KMS provider and customer separation model.
- Confirm there are no identifiers in trace tags (Aisha's note says they strip IDs, but we need a sample sanitized trace payload or the sanitization script description).
- Request a short written assurance that no debug logs containing request headers will be sent to EdgeChain.

If Observic can provide the requested redacted auditor pages and a sample sanitized trace (redacted), we can sign off and update FinPay procurement with the change notice. If not, we will request Observic to postpone until they can produce the items.

I'll draft a short checklist we can send to Aisha.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Director, Security Compliance
Redwood Inference

Can Observic provide a one-page amendment draft? 

If Observic can provide the redacted SOC2 pages and the sanitized trace sample by EOD Nov 18, Redwood + FinPay legal will review and aim to acknowledge the change before Nov 19. Otherwise, we'll request Observic to hold the cutover.

If useful, we can stand up a 15-minute call tomorrow (Nov 17) at 09:30 PST to walk the bundle.
